{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABYfo5QQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhCD8Ec", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 35, "title": "Support current-renderer RendererReferenceNode toneMappingExposure instances", "body": "## Problem

The Draft v2.0 default plugins already round-trip the **exact shared** TSL object `toneMappingExposure`, but independently constructed ordinary `RendererReferenceNode` instances are unsupported. Three.js r186 creates the shared object using `rendererReference('toneMappingExposure', 'float')`, and the ordinary class selects either an explicit renderer or the active `NodeFrame` / `NodeBuilder` renderer.

A narrow *current-renderer* adapter can transport the native property selector without freezing renderer state or introducing a renderer ID into glTF. Supporting a shared singleton by name is **not** proof that a separately constructed instance round-trips: preserve the distinction and its graph identity.

## Expected outcome

1. **Audit Three.js r186** and recheck the current stable Three.js during implementation: `RendererReferenceNode`, its `ReferenceBaseNode` superclass, `ToneMappingNode.toneMappingExposure`, `NodeFrame` updates, default `renderGroup`, `Node.serialize()/getSerializeChildren()`, `UniformNode` creation, and GLSL/WGSL setup. Establish exact constructor, mutable, cached and lifecycle state, including behavior before/after shader compilation.
2. Extend the **existing default exporter serializer and loader resolver** with a paired, data-only adapter for ordinary `RendererReferenceNode` instances using exactly:
   - `property === 'toneMappingExposure'` and `uniformType === 'float'`;
   - `renderer === null` and no foreign `object` / external renderer binding;
   - native supported default `renderGroup` and update scheduling, with only base fields whose fidelity is demonstrably preserved.
   Use the native Three.js class, native reference/update methods and existing graph traversal; do **not** reimplement exposure calculations or shader code.
3. Save only the validated property/type and any verified constructor/base state in node arguments; **never save the current renderer's exposure value** as a fixed literal or serialize a renderer object. Reconstruct an independently constructed node bound to the **consumer's active renderer**; its value must remain live as `renderer.toneMappingExposure` changes.
4. Preserve exact shared TSL `toneMappingExposure` identity through the pre-existing singleton path. Ordinary instances must remain independent from that singleton, with node identity and references shared correctly *within* each material graph across two export/import rounds. Do not retarget ordinary instances to the shared object simply to simplify reconstruction.
5. Validate native caches, internal uniform/group and update state where necessary without serializing generated child/internal runtime nodes. Preserve native semantics for built and unbuilt instances when safely possible. Reject custom callback methods, unknown meaningful child links/fields, changed update frequencies, unsupported groups, subclasses masquerading as native classes, and malformed operation arguments on export.
6. Import must reject unknown property/type combinations, unexpected args/links, dangling references, cycles, invalid unreachable definitions and other malformed graphs **atomically**: retain the entire ordinary glTF material, its other supported material extensions, and material clones; never publish a partially rebuilt TSL graph.
7. Clearly **defer**: explicit/non-null renderers, other renderer properties and value types (until audited), nested property paths, custom external binding IDs, custom uniform groups, callbacks and renderer ownership/scheduling. Explain the exact future paired resolver/registry contract if an application wishes to bind a specific external renderer. A file must never contain arbitrary JS/GLSL/WGSL or a renderer instance.

Keep Draft v2.0, `materialType`, ordinary material coexistence, the current v1.0 removal, and existing plugin architecture unchanged. No Three.js core changes unless the actual plugin hooks prove insufficient.

## Context and reproduction

- [Draft v2.0 specification](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md)
- [Current coverage matrix: explicit references](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md)
- [Current material/model reference audit](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/reference-node-support.md)
- [Uniform-group identity and lifecycle audit (#27)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/uniform-group-support.md)
- [Default exporter serializer](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/defaultNodeSerializer.ts)
- [Default loader resolver](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/defaultNodeResolver.ts)
- [Existing paired reference adapters](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/referenceNodes.ts)
- [Integration suites](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/demo/test)
- [Three.js r186 RendererReferenceNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/RendererReferenceNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 ReferenceBaseNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/ReferenceBaseNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 ToneMappingNode (shared toneMappingExposure)](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/display/ToneMappingNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 NodeFrame](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/core/NodeFrame.js)

Representative use case: an ordinary `rendererReference('toneMappingExposure', 'float')` placed in a supported NodeMaterial expression. After GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader, a new ordinary instance must read the current renderer's changing exposure through Three.js's normal update flow. The existing `toneMappingExposure` singleton must still round-trip by exact identity.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the audited current Three.js version, ordinary-instance constructor/field/updater behavior and exact supported/unsupported variants, with source-level deferral reasons.
- [ ] Implement paired default exporter/loader support for the verified current-renderer `toneMappingExposure`/float subset, using existing plugins and the native TSL stack. Preserve ordinary node identity and the shared singleton path separately.
- [ ] Add **real** GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader → GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader JSON glTF and representative GLB integration tests for distinct ordinary instances, graph sharing, material entrypoints, ordinary glTF material properties and other supported material extensions.
- [ ] Test native active-renderer selection and subsequent exposure changes using real Three.js `NodeFrame`/reference methods (or a verified native-equivalent harness). Test before/after import and built/unbuilt states. Compare GLSL/WGSL shader setup/analyze/generate and native uniform/group behavior where feasible; distinguish Node-side checks from hardware rendering.
- [ ] Add negative export/import cases for an explicit foreign renderer, wrong property/type, extra args/links/fields, callbacks, custom schedules/groups, broken references, cycles, invalid unreachable definitions and whole-material fallback (including clones/other material extensions).
- [ ] Update the coverage matrix, affected loader/exporter READMEs and a focused source/validation audit with precise supported and deferred boundaries; leave Draft v2.0 unchanged and do not restore v1.0.
- [ ] Run and report the actual full demo tests, loader/exporter builds, demo typecheck/build and `git diff --check`, including warnings, failures, skips and any unperformed validations. There is no root test command.

## Optional validation

Browser WebGL/WebGPU visual smoke tests with a live renderer and changing exposure. If not performed, explicitly state that Node-side shader generation/runtime checks do not prove GPU compilation or pixel behavior.

## Required post-merge verification

None. **Do not publish npm packages or bump their versions in this issue.** The maintainer performs `npm publish` manually as a separate release step.
